observed.title: Assert the discounted total
observed.body:
**Assert the discounted total**

The `toBeDefined()` assertion passes if SAVE10 returns the undiscounted total or another incorrect defined value. Assert the expected total instead:
```ts
expect(applyCoupon(100, 'SAVE10')).toBe(90);
```

<details><summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

kind: weak_test, confidence: high
</details>

## SpecGuard

Reviewed: Tests: 3 missing, 1 weak · Standards: 0 · Layering: 0; 4 inline, 0 file-level, 0 in summary.

Unit evidence: 0/5 obligations (static review; tests not executed).

_Engine: copilot_

**Standards tooling: not_configured.** Commit: 84dac07c7e85201f82c2a91db89959ad2ffc8859. 


**Requirements source:** PR body

| Criterion | Source / original wording | Obligations | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | PR body: Add applyCoupon, which applies a coupon code to an order total. | X1 | 0/1 obligations covered (not fully covered). The PR body supplies one criterion: applying a coupon code to an order total. |

**Coding standards: checked.** Assessed the provided rule file and its applyTo scope; it applies only to src/** and eval/*.js, not eval-sandbox/ts2, so no coding rules apply to these changes. Sources: .github/instructions/specguard.instructions.md.

**Test layers: checked.** Inspected the Vitest tests and repository-wide matches across test files. The matching tests are isolated calls to a pure exported function, so they are unit-layer evidence; no component, integration, or end-to-end evidence or pushdown candidate was found.

| Obligation | Source / behaviour | Assertion evidence / layer | Status / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1: applyCoupon applies a coupon code to an order total. | PR body; eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.ts:5 —   return Math.round(total * (1 - rate) * 100) / 100; | unit: eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.test.ts:6 —     expect(applyCoupon(100, 'SAVE10')).toBeDefined(); (assertion; Calls applyCoupon for SAVE10 but checks only that the result is defined, not that the coupon changes the total as required.) | weak_test: The unit assertion passes for an undiscounted or otherwise incorrect defined result. A repository-wide search for applyCoupon, SAVE10, and HALF found only this test and an identical test in eval/cases/ts2/head/coupon.test.ts; neither asserts the resulting total. |
| B1: SAVE10 reduces the total by 10%. | from behaviour; eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.ts:1 — const COUPON_RATES: Record<string, number> = { SAVE10: 0.1, HALF: 0.5 }; | unit: eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.test.ts:6 —     expect(applyCoupon(100, 'SAVE10')).toBeDefined(); (assertion; Exercises SAVE10, but the defined-value assertion would survive a wrong discount rate or an unchanged total.) | weak_test: The SAVE10 input is exercised, but the assertion does not check its expected discounted total; mutations that change or remove the discount can still pass. |
| B2: HALF reduces the total by 50%. | from behaviour; eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.ts:1 — const COUPON_RATES: Record<string, number> = { SAVE10: 0.1, HALF: 0.5 }; | unit: eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.test.ts:6 —     expect(applyCoupon(100, 'SAVE10')).toBeDefined(); (no_assertion; The assertion invokes SAVE10, not HALF, and provides no assertion for the HALF rate.) | missing_test: The repository-wide search for applyCoupon, HALF, and related coupon tests found no unit assertion using HALF. |
| B3: An unknown coupon code leaves the total unchanged. | from behaviour; eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.ts:4 —   const rate = COUPON_RATES[code] ?? 0; | unit: eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.test.ts:6 —     expect(applyCoupon(100, 'SAVE10')).toBeDefined(); (no_assertion; The assertion invokes SAVE10, not an unknown code, and does not check fallback behavior.) | missing_test: The repository-wide search for applyCoupon and coupon tests found no unit assertion using an unknown code or checking the unchanged-total fallback. |
| B4: The discounted total is rounded to cents. | from behaviour; eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.ts:5 —   return Math.round(total * (1 - rate) * 100) / 100; | unit: eval-sandbox/ts2/coupon.test.ts:6 —     expect(applyCoupon(100, 'SAVE10')).toBeDefined(); (no_assertion; The assertion uses an input with a whole-number discounted result and does not check cent rounding.) | missing_test: The repository-wide search for applyCoupon and coupon tests found no unit assertion with a fractional discounted result that verifies cent rounding. |

## SpecGuard

Reviewed: Tests: 3 missing, 0 weak · Standards: 0 · Layering: 0; 3 inline, 0 file-level, 0 in summary.

Unit evidence: 1/4 obligations (static review; tests not executed).

_Engine: copilot_

**Standards tooling: not_configured.** Commit: 95433fe6d986d7ef18a68c6717eeca02230718f4. 


**Requirements source:** PR body

| Criterion | Source / original wording | Obligations | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | PR body: It returns the response when a fetch attempt succeeds. | R1 | 1/1 obligations covered. The unit assertion checks that a successful fetch returns the exact response object. |
| R2 | PR body: A network error is retried until `retries` attempts have been made (default 3). | R2a, R2b | 0/2 obligations covered (not fully covered). Assessed the configured retry limit and the default of three attempts as separate testable behaviors. |
| R3 | PR body: After `retries` failed attempts it throws the last error. | R3 | 0/1 obligations covered (not fully covered). The criterion requires verifying that the final rejected attempt's error is thrown. |

**Coding standards: checked.** Reviewed the listed rule file; its applyTo pattern (src/**,eval/*.js) excludes both changed eval-sandbox/js2 files, so no rules from it apply to these changes. Sources: .github/instructions/specguard.instructions.md.

**Test layers: checked.** Inspected the Jest ESM package configuration and searched test/spec files across the repository. The changed test uses a mocked global fetch and calls the exported function directly, so it is unit-level evidence; no component, integration, or end-to-end coverage for this function was found. The behavior has a direct public unit seam and no higher-layer logic to push down.

| Obligation | Source / behaviour | Assertion evidence / layer | Status / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1: Return the response when a fetch attempt succeeds. | PR body; eval-sandbox/js2/fetchWithRetry.js:5 —       return await fetch(url); | unit: eval-sandbox/js2/fetchWithRetry.spec.js:11 —   await expect(fetchWithRetry('https://api.test/items')).resolves.toBe(response); (assertion; When the first fetch succeeds, the function resolves to the same response object.) | covered: The test mocks the external fetch boundary to succeed and asserts the exact returned response through the public function. |
| R2a: Retry network errors up to the configured attempt count. | PR body; eval-sandbox/js2/fetchWithRetry.js:3 —   for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= retries; attempt++) { | unit: eval-sandbox/js2/fetchWithRetry.spec.js:11 —   await expect(fetchWithRetry('https://api.test/items')).resolves.toBe(response); (no_assertion; This assertion covers a successful first attempt only; it does not assert retry behavior or attempt count.) | missing_test: A repository-wide search of test and spec files found only first-attempt success coverage; no unit assertion exercises a network failure or verifies the configured attempt count. |
| R2b: Use three attempts when the retry count is omitted. | PR body; eval-sandbox/js2/fetchWithRetry.js:1 — export async function fetchWithRetry(url, { retries = 3 } = {}) { | unit: eval-sandbox/js2/fetchWithRetry.spec.js:11 —   await expect(fetchWithRetry('https://api.test/items')).resolves.toBe(response); (no_assertion; This assertion supplies no failure and does not check the default number of attempts.) | missing_test: A repository-wide search of test and spec files found no unit assertion that omits retries and verifies the default attempt count. |
| R3: Throw the error from the final failed attempt. | PR body; eval-sandbox/js2/fetchWithRetry.js:7 —       lastError = error; | unit: eval-sandbox/js2/fetchWithRetry.spec.js:11 —   await expect(fetchWithRetry('https://api.test/items')).resolves.toBe(response); (no_assertion; This assertion covers a successful attempt and makes no assertion about errors after failed attempts.) | missing_test: A repository-wide search of test and spec files found no unit assertion for repeated failures or the identity of the final error. |
